page0.text: Before that, there's just one more conversation.

page1.text:
When they get out of the forest and day breaks...
Before they head to the church, the girl tells him the fact that she kept hidden.

page2.text:
"I'll tell you this now, but the pendant that you gave back to me is one of a kind."
She doesn't say what that means, and he doesn't pursue it further.
That is because that is an unnecessary matter when they are about to fight their biggest enemy... Caster.

page3.text:
Only one pendant.
The one that he found in her room and returned to her.
The one that he picked up that night and put into his desk.
Now is not the time to be pursuing that contradiction.

page4.text:
"...That's all I have to say.
The pendant that you found in my room is something Archer returned to me on the day you were stabbed by Lancer.
I just assumed that was something that he picked up."

page5.text:
The decisive battle is near.
The roof of the tall church can be seen in the corner, when looking up at the sky.

page6.text:
Tohsaka says she wants to confirm things one last time.
Our roles are decided.
Lancer will draw Archer and Saber away from Caster.
We will use that opening to fight Caster.

page7.text:
In response to Lancer sarcastically asking if we'd be able to defeat Caster...
"...Yeah. I think I can outwit Caster if I can fight her one-on-one."
Tohsaka replies with confidence.

page8.text:
...I don't know what she means by outwitting her.
She wouldn't tell us even if we asked, so it must be a strategy that has a lower success rate if she tells her allies.

page9.text:
Then, all I need to do is fulfill Tohsaka's demands.
I will keep Kuzuki from protecting Caster no matter what.
I'll Project his swords however many times is necessary to do that.

page10.text:
...I close my eyes and dive inside myself.
The Magic Circuit that flows inside me is stable.
Magecraft beyond one's capacity will destroy the user themselves.
The first time, half of my body went numb.
The second time's Projection was surprisingly easy and had no effect on my body.
There's no guarantee that the third time will be the same, but I think there should be no problem if it's just copying his swords.

page11.text:
My body is stable.
Through sheer awareness alone, I have access to the Magic Circuits that were so difficult to create before.
It's like there's a fake nerve behind my normal nerve, and I'm able to reverse them with just the press of a button.
There's part of me that wants to believe it's because I got used to it.

page12.text:
I can easily prepare the swords.
Projection has become my primary weapon.
It's improved greatly compared to ten days ago.
Not only has the control of my Magic Circuits improved, but even my sword technique has improved.

page13.text:
"..."
The reason behind it...
I stop myself from thinking about the reason.
It's top priority to defeat Caster and get Saber back.

page14.text:
Asking myself stupid questions can come after the battle.
My headache gets worse the closer I get to the church.
It's just like when I was looking for Tohsaka, but I stop thinking about that.

page15.text:
The sunrise is gray.
The sunlight is blocked by the clouds, sealing the dawn's brightness.
The sky above is cloudy.
The sky is closer to black than gray and reminds me of that time ten years ago.

page16.text:
Is it going to start raining soon?
A dull white sky.
That man was standing under the cloudy sky that smelled like it had just stopped raining.

page17.text:
"I knew you would come."
He stares at Tohsaka with cool eyes.
...
Tohsaka doesn't say anything and stares back at Archer.

page18.text:
"So, what is the plan you've prepared? You're not the type to challenge someone without one."
"Yeah. You're fighting me."

page19.text:
"I'm surprised. It's only been a few days since you lost me, and you already made a contract with a new Servant?
Good grief. I'm not one to talk, but you're quite fickle. Maybe cutting ties with you was the right thing to do."
"Ugh—!"

page20.text:
"...It's fine, Shirou. Don't let him provoke you."
She stops me, still staring at Archer.
...But, it's obvious looking at her face.
Even if she knows he's provoking her, it doesn't change the fact that those words hurt for Tohsaka.

page21.text: "...Heh. I didn't like you from the start, but...it seems you're rotten to your core."

page22.text:
"Oh. Does betrayal get on your nerves, Lancer? You're not even the one who got betrayed. How faithful of you."
"...I'm not supporting the young lady.
I just don't like how there are Servants like you."

page23.text:
"A hero's pride, huh? Geez, everyone says the same thing.
Even that Caster had such a ridiculous thing. What honor do you have to protect when you're dead?
To be honest, I can't understand how you people think."

page24.text: "Yeah, you don't have to. I'll save you the trouble."

page25.text:
Conversation ceases between the two of them.
All that's left is Lancer's sharp intent to kill,
and Archer's calm intent to kill.

page26.text:
...
...They are about ten meters apart.
The knight in red and knight in blue confronting each other is like a reenactment of that night.

page27.text:
"Lancer."
Tohsaka calls to the blue back.

page28.text:
"You two go inside. I'll catch up once I beat this guy."
"...I know. But Lancer, Archer is—"
"Yeah, I'll go easy on him. I need for him to get on his knees and apologize to you."
Without looking back, he smiles while still staring at Archer.

page29.text:
"...Thanks.
I'm glad you're the one who came to help us."

page30.text:
We go around the two and run to the church.
Archer, the guard, casually lets us go through.
No, he had to let us through.

page31.text:
Archer is already confronting Lancer.
If he gave us attention in such a situation, he would get stabbed in the chest by Lancer the next moment.
Either he doesn't let us go but gets attacked by Lancer, or he lets us go but confronts Lancer.
If he is really guarding this place, the choice should be obvious.

page32.text:
We run around the courtyard and open the door to the church without hesitation.
Behind us...

page33.text:
"...Geez. This is troublesome."
"What is, Lancer?"
"Well, I can't go easy after she thanks me like that.
That's troubling, right? She's a great Master, but I'm not one who is able to betray my Master readily."
